channel.description: A permanent record of Polyemergence coverage across AI and emerging technology, organized by Singapore publication date.

item.title: Analysts debate Nvidia's future after Jensen Huang's departure
item.description:
Following media reports regarding personal conduct, Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia's CEO, ending a 33-year run that turned the chip maker into a US$4 trillion giant. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO while the board conducts a search for a permanent successor.
Financial institutions and industry experts have drawn parallels to Apple's historical transitions. Goldman Sachs analysts noted that while both companies shared visionary leadership and deep-rooted innovation cultures, Huang's sudden departure could make it harder for Nvidia to operate with its previous agility. They predict medium-term stock volatility as the market seeks a new valuation multiple.
Industry figures and political leaders have also weighed in. Elon Musk criticized the removal of powerful founders, citing Apple and Uber as cautionary tales. Meanwhile, some analysts and political figures, including US President Donald Trump, floated the idea of former Apple CEO Tim Cook taking the helm, noting Cook's operational strengths in supply chain management, though experts warn that replacing Huang's unique role in driving cutting-edge AI technology remains an unprecedented challenge.

item.title: AI DJs Kill the Music Groove
item.description: The Problem with AI Commentary YouTube Music and Spotify have both rolled out experimental AI DJ features designed to talk between tracks, explain upcoming music, and mimic human casualness. However, according to a Wired software reporter, these additions often disrupt the flow of music rather than enhance it. Flawed Execution and Awkward Voices Testing both platforms revealed consistent issues. YouTube Music's experimental DJ delivered lengthy, hollow paragraphs of analysis and even mispronounced artist names, while also occasionally playing the wrong track version. Meanwhile, Spotify's updated AI voices leaned heavily into synthetic filler words like "you know," triggering an uncanny valley reaction for the listener despite the company claiming high user retention rates.

item.title: Top scorer in South Korea tax exam admits using AI to cheat
item.description:
According to reports, the candidate identified as Han ranked first in both rounds of South Korea's tax accountant qualification exams held in April and July. In the first round, he scored 397.5 out of 400 points, getting only one question wrong out of 160. Initially, he denied accusations of cheating with smart glasses, but he later confessed through his lawyer on a YouTube channel, stating that he used a microcamera to photograph exam questions, sent them to an AI tool, and checked answers on a smartphone. He has since submitted a written confession to the Seoul metropolitan police agency.
The incident has severely rattled South Korea, where standardized testing heavily dictates social mobility. With the annual national college entrance exam approaching, the presidential office and prime minister's office have stepped in, holding emergency meetings and vowing to implement strict countermeasures to ensure test fairness.

item.title: As Gemini is called US Doubao, Zhang Yiming lives as China's Brin
item.description: The Return of Founders Faced with the paradigm shift of artificial intelligence, traditional corporate management structures struggle with long-term and high-uncertainty research cycles. This has driven the founder mode back into mainstream tech management. Google's Sergey Brin and ByteDance's Zhang Yiming have both re-engaged deeply with core technical teams to bypass bureaucratic inertia and accelerate decision-making. Different Strategies, Same Goal While both founders are heavily invested in AI, their tactical approaches differ. Brin emphasizes speed, putting in long hours at the Google office to push model evolution. Meanwhile, Zhang Yiming adopts a patient stance with ByteDance's Seed team, focusing on building solid fundamentals rather than rushing for quick fixes. Despite these tactical differences, both are locking horns with native AI powerhouses with a 2030 time horizon.

item.title: Should you invest in AI stocks now? Nvidia's slump, Anthropic's IPO and 5 strategies to consider
item.description: Market Context and Contrasting Signals Recent market developments highlight a shift in the artificial intelligence sector. Nvidia Corp. experienced its worst weekly performance since April 2025, with shares dropping 13% over five trading days, following the ouster of Jensen Huang. Conversely, Anthropic PBC's proposed initial public offering and private placement drew massive interest, attracting orders six times the available shares and aiming for a massive valuation. Growth and Ecosystem Risks According to Blue Aster Capital's Sidharth Sogani Jain, Anthropic's annualised revenue run rate has surged significantly, proving the real commercial demand for AI applications. However, Jain cautions that rapid top-line growth does not guarantee immediate profitability, especially given Anthropic's substantial operating losses and high valuation. Furthermore, the interconnected nature of the ecosystem—where Nvidia acts as both a key hardware supplier and a proposed investor in Anthropic—means that financial risks can easily spill over between major players. Investment Strategies To navigate this shifting landscape, experts recommend five practical steps: audit your current portfolio exposure, stagger your investments over several months rather than lump-sum buying, diversify across different layers of the AI stack, avoid blindly chasing oversubscribed IPOs like Anthropic, and steer clear of high leverage during periods of short-term market volatility.

item.title: AI Meets America's New World: Why Data Centers Face a Wave of Delays and Backlash
item.description: The recent US midterm elections have reshaped the political and economic landscape surrounding artificial intelligence, shining a spotlight on the friction between tech expansion and local communities. With Democrats gaining control of both houses of Congress and key regional shifts, such as Gina Hinojosa winning the Texas governorship, the approval process for massive data center projects has hit significant roadblocks. ## Key Details Industry insiders note that public pushback is no longer a secondary concern; it has become a primary risk factor. Residents are increasingly worried about rising utility bills, water scarcity, and environmental impacts. Although large tech companies and cloud providers are willing to shoulder grid and water system upgrades, the extended legislative cycles, potential tax burdens, and strict local negotiations could drive up overall data center construction costs by 10% to 20%. Furthermore, rigorous permit requirements, such as air pollution and grid interconnection approvals, threaten to delay or even cancel planned projects over the next year. Industry Impact Despite supply-side slowdowns and a volatile market reaction that has hammered upstream hardware stocks, tech executives argue that underlying computing demand remains exceptionally high. Hyperscalers continue to report massive order backlogs, and token consumption metrics show robust growth. However, the short-term mismatch between planned infrastructure and actual deployment timelines will force the industry to re-evaluate capital expenditures, potentially shifting pricing power to existing data center operators while squeezing upstream suppliers.

item.title: Chinese AI giants start stripping hacking skills from open models to curb risks
item.description: Background With artificial intelligence models becoming powerful enough to autonomously develop sophisticated cyber exploits, companies face mounting risks of misuse. Unlike closed-source models where developers can monitor user activity and ban violators, open-weight models allow anyone with sufficient hardware to download and modify the software, making safety by design a critical priority. Details To address this, Chinese technology giant Tencent stripped its latest Hy4 model of cyber-hacking capabilities while retaining defense features, following a similar move by Moonshot AI in October. Instead of abandoning open weights, companies are selectively removing offensive cyber data during training. However, experts note a clear trade-off: Moonshot AI acknowledged that its filtered model scored 81 percent on an internal security benchmark, compared with 90.5 percent for the unrestricted version. Furthermore, cybersecurity skills are dual-use, meaning defense tools can still potentially be exploited by malicious actors. Impact This emerging safety practice highlights the difficult balancing act Chinese AI firms face as they try to maintain their market edge without violating tightening government export controls and risk thresholds. While targeted restrictions may weaken specialized security performance, broader competitiveness will still rely on coding quality, cost, and deployment flexibility.

item.title: v0.83.0-dev20261115: Tenstorrent TT-Metal Open Source AI Hardware Software Stack Update
item.description:
Low-Level Kernel and Core Optimizations
According to the release notes, the development team has focused heavily on refining low-level kernels (LLK). This includes introducing fused BF16 kernels for various mathematical operations, which substantially reduce execution overhead compared to previous versions. Furthermore, core recovery mechanisms and performance test harnesses have been updated to ensure greater stability during intensive hardware workloads. Metalium Core and Hardware Acceleration
The Metalium core infrastructure receives key upgrades, including the migration of crucial Metal 2.0 headers to the stable API. Notably, Blackhole host-to-device socket writes into Tensix L1 memory have been accelerated, achieving up to roughly fourteen times faster performance for large pages, which helps reduce data bottlenecking. TT-NN and Model Support
The update expands model support and optimizations for prominent architectures such as DeepSeek, MiniMax, GLM, and Kimi-K3. Additions include optimized prefill stages, dynamic sequence length handling, and refined tensor operations, ensuring better execution efficiency on Tenstorrent hardware configurations.

item.title: Making Quantum SDKs More Accessible: Lessons from Contributing to Qiskit
item.description: The Documentation Gap in Quantum SDKs Quantum Software Development Kits like Qiskit, Google Cirq, and PennyLane provide essential tools for building quantum programs. However, functional software often suffers from poor documentation. A 2025 study involving 251 practitioners found that over 60% learn quantum languages from official documentation, with inadequate examples cited as a major challenge. Outdated API versions and abstract mathematical representations compound the difficulty for conventional software developers entering the field. Practical Fixes and the Role of Testing Drawing from her experience as a junior developer contributing to Qiskit, Amos investigated a reported issue regarding confusing API references. She discovered discrepancies such as undocumented rotation bases and typos in gate mappings. By updating the documentation and writing test coverage for missing cases, her pull request was successfully merged, proving that thorough testing ensures software implementation aligns with documentation. Impact on Developer Experience The experience highlights that lowering the barriers to entry in quantum computing requires more than just raw technical capabilities. Ensuring that documentation, tests, and code are perfectly aligned successfully eliminates avoidable confusion and makes complex quantum tools more accessible to a broader community.

item.title: Elon Musk and thousands of others sign petition demanding Nvidia bring back ousted CEO Jensen Huang
item.description: Background Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday following his confession to an extramarital affair with a chip executive identified by U.S. intelligence as a suspected Chinese spy, with media reports also indicating multiple other affairs. Petition Details By Saturday afternoon, a petition demanding Huang's reinstatement attracted over 115,000 signatures. The signatories include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders, alongside high-profile tech figures like Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney. The petition argues that Huang was removed without meaningful due process and calls for an independent investigation. Industry Impact Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO during the search for a permanent replacement. Following the leadership shakeup, Nvidia's stock fell 2%, and analysts expect Huang's departure to leave a significant gap in overall AI industry funding.

item.title: Australian senator warns artists' copyright and environment must not be sacrificed for AI
item.description:
Australian Liberal senator Andrew McLachlan has expressed strong concerns regarding the approach of both major political parties toward AI policy, specifically regarding potential changes to copyright law and the rapid expansion of datacentres.
McLachlan argued that watering down copyright to allow AI companies to scrape creative works amounts to treating machines as more valuable than human art, pointing out that constitutional challenges regarding the illegal acquisition of property are being mooted. While tech firms like Anthropic advocate for an 'opt-out' model to ingest music, books, and journalism, local recording industries and several lawmakers have pushed back.
Beyond copyright, McLachlan and environmental groups highlighted that the massive growth of datacentres will likely increase carbon emissions and household energy bills, while threatening biodiversity. The federal government is expected to unveil a comprehensive AI policy package before the end of the year, which includes measures for a new AI safety regulator.

item.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's downfall rocks Trump administration and AI industry
item.description: The Collapse of a Central Pillar The November departure of Nvidia's powerful leader Jensen Huang, following partly-acknowledged personal scandals, has destabilized the driving force of the global artificial intelligence revolution. As the mastermind behind a massive business ecosystem fueled by astronomical profits, Huang built a highly centralized corporate structure, leaving behind a difficult-to-fill power vacuum and exposing the structural risks of reliance on larger-than-life tech leaders. Public Backlash and Political Consensus The shockwave coincides with a growing public unease over the tech industry's accelerationist approach, particularly regarding energy-hungry data centers that create few local jobs. In a deeply polarized United States, voter resistance to these facilities has unexpectedly forged a rare bipartisan consensus, with local communities pushing back against reckless expansion. Regulatory and Government Turbulence In the short term, the Trump administration faces mounting pressure to clarify the lenient export policies that previously allowed Nvidia considerable leeway in shipping advanced chips to China. Internal tensions have already surfaced between Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick regarding export restrictions, signaling impending turbulence for tech policy.

item.title: Goal Engineering: The Future of Designing AI Agents
item.description: According to LangChain Blog: Background and Challenges As AI agents transition from simple text generation and tool calling to executing full, open-ended tasks, the way we design their scope matters immensely. Pointing agents in the wrong direction wastes valuable tokens. A major bottleneck in agent performance is a lack of the right context, especially tacit knowledge that lives only inside human heads and cannot be found in written documents. The Role of Feedback and UX When agents tackle subjective tasks alongside humans, they need constant feedback to learn brand tastes, strategic preferences, and nuanced behaviors. Building an intuitive and delightful UX for reviewing agent work is essential. Since the bottleneck for agent performance is learning from feedback, optimizing the ease and quality of feedback collection unlocks long-horizon capabilities. Case Study: Actively AI Actively AI initially designed sales agents on a per-account basis, giving each agent the goal of moving a single prospective customer forward. However, they found that salespeople suffered from constant context switching and struggled to share learnings across different accounts. In their second iteration, Actively shifted to "motions", where agents handle specific jobs to be done, such as outbounding or deal progression, across multiple accounts. This aligned the workflow with how humans naturally review and provide feedback, allowing agents to learn much more quickly while background agents gather objective account data.

item.title: Lynxel launches two LMS resin 3D printers supporting high viscosity
item.description: Background and Technology According to Nanjixiong, tree-dimensional printing startup Lynxel has developed a layer-membrane stereolithography (LMS) platform. Traditional desktop resin printers often struggle with thick formulas because they rely on passive fluid flow. The LMS platform uses an active moving film to spread and feed resin, which helps control separation forces and allows the equipment to handle standard resins as well as higher viscosity, flexible, and composite materials up to 300,000 cP. Printer Models and Features The company is preparing two initial devices for a Kickstarter pre-sale campaign, though final pricing and delivery timelines are not yet disclosed. The LynBeam LB1 acts as the primary functional model with a build volume of 200×400×300 mm. Meanwhile, the LynChrom LC1 incorporates an integrated CMYK inkjet system to perform direct full-color surface printing during the build process, reducing the need for manual painting afterward. Software and Exhibition The companion software, Lynxel Studio, handles model preparation and includes an AI assistant named Lenny. Lynxel plans to demonstrate the LMS platform and display physical samples at the upcoming Formnext 2026 exhibition in Frankfurt.

item.title: Don’t try to sell printers: HP’s additive manufacturing sales strategy
item.description: 产能大扩张与生产占比变化 ADDMAN通过收购等动作，正计划将其多射流熔融（MJF）3D打印机舰队扩充至125台以上。惠普全球销售负责人弗朗索瓦·米内克指出，服务商的工作重心已经发生了明显转变，从过去大约各占一半的原型制作与生产，演变为如今生产业务占据约80%的业务量。 技术改进与参数开放 为了满足工业量产的要求，惠普在5600系列上提升了多台设备之间的打印一致性。此外，惠普还打破了过去的封闭限制，允许操作员访问35个工艺参数（如层厚和喷头设置），让不同的服务商能够根据自身需求开发出独特的打印模式。 卖设备不如做应用 米内克强调，单纯向客户推销打印机效果有限，关键在于帮助终端客户开发真正有价值的杀手级应用，例如无人机零件或医用头盔。当制造企业通过3D打印大幅缩短了组装时间并产生持续的量产需求时，订单自然会流向服务商，从而最终带动打印机设备的销售。

item.title: Jensen Huang leaves Nvidia after 33 years
item.description: The Exit and Its Background On January 6th, 2025, Jensen Huang made his final high-profile appearance as Nvidia's CEO. Shortly after, he left the company he cofounded 33 years ago amid reports of chip smuggling scandals and personal misconduct. As the leader of the world's most valuable chipmaker, Huang was unique in his absolute centralization of power, with around 60 employees reporting directly to him. Business and Technology Impact Industry analysts emphasize that Nvidia's immediate future is not in jeopardy. The company's hardware roadmap and manufacturing partnerships are locked in through 2027, and its supply chain dominance remains unmatched. However, experts note that Huang was irreplaceable as a culture setter and risk-taker who pushed through historical gambles like the CUDA platform, which ultimately powered the modern AI boom. The Search for a Successor Finding a new CEO will be difficult because Huang operated without deputies and built the entire organization around himself. Observers believe the company will likely need to look outside for a leader who can maintain investor confidence and protect the CUDA ecosystem during this transitional vacuum.

item.title: Jensen Huang Steps Down as NVIDIA CEO, Opening the Door for AMD and Google
item.description:
NVIDIA shares fell 4.34% following the abrupt resignation of CEO Jensen Huang, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO. Analysts note that Huang's deep personal relationships and aggressive financing strategies were central to NVIDIA's market dominance, and his departure creates a strategic and diplomatic vacuum that could slow down new bilateral deals.
At the same time, rival AMD is seeing massive momentum. CEO Lisa Su was named Yahoo Finance's 2026 CEO of the Year, with AMD shares up nearly 139% year-to-date. AMD has secured multi-generation hardware agreements with OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic, alongside acquiring spatial intelligence startup World Labs for $8.2 billion.
Google is also scaling its TPU business, reporting over 100 significant cloud customers and partnering with Oracle to offer TPUs outside its own cloud infrastructure from 2027. While NVIDIA's CUDA ecosystem remains a strong moat, the combination of leadership transition and stricter export rules is prompting buyers to accelerate their adoption of custom silicon and alternative accelerators.

item.title: New method solves degradation in copper-plated solar cells
item.description: Background To make solar panels cheaper, scientists are trying to replace expensive silver with copper in silicon heterojunction (HJT) solar cells. However, applying the necessary photoresist layer through screen printing causes a gradual efficiency decline over thousands of printing cycles, dropping conversion efficiency in commercial production. Details and Discovery According to the researchers, traditional silver paste uses screens with small openings and thick emulsion coverage, so the mesh rarely touches the wafer directly. In contrast, photoresist application uses an open mesh that slams directly against the wafer surface. Using confocal microscopy, the team discovered that progressive wear of the screen mesh knuckles increases mechanical stress, damaging the delicate passivation layers underneath. Solution and Impact To fix this, the team tested an emulsion buffer layer on the screen. An optimal coverage ratio of 4.7% successfully prevented direct contact between the mesh and the wafer. This reduced minority carrier lifetime degradation to just 0.41% after 10,000 cycles, offering a practical way to improve manufacturing reliability for copper-plated solar cells.

item.title: Researchers Find a Better Way to Design Long-Lasting Sodium Battery Cathodes
item.description: Research Background O3-type layered oxides are promising candidates for sodium-ion battery cathodes because they offer high capacity and initial sodium content. However, operating them at high voltages causes deep sodium extraction, which weakens electrostatic screening and triggers harmful phase transitions and lattice degradation. Traditional dopant selection has relied mostly on average ionic radii or valence states, which fail to capture local bonding heterogeneity. Method and Findings Published in JACS on October 20, 2026, by a team including Nankai University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences, the study introduces an ionic field strength descriptor to quantify local disparities among transition metal cations. By comparing low- and high-disparity materials, the researchers demonstrated that the low-disparity cathode follows a more reversible phase evolution path, avoids extra high-voltage phase changes, and exhibits smaller lattice parameter shifts during desodiation. Synchrotron X-ray and strain mapping further confirmed reduced local coordination disorder and suppressed strain accumulation. Practical Implications This approach transforms dopant selection from an empirical search into a quantitative design task. While the framework shows promise for accelerating cathode development in stationary storage and high-voltage sodium-ion batteries, the authors note that it still requires validation across broader compositions and practical full-cell conditions before commercial deployment.

item.title: AI Is Rocking the Literary World
item.description: The Rise of AI Authors Some self-published authors are leveraging generative AI to rapidly produce books, navigating platforms like Kindle Unlimited where high output is rewarded. Studies estimate that a significant portion of recent self-published books contain AI-generated text, though writers note that understanding structure and craft remains essential for success. Scandals and Accusations Mainstream publishing is facing a period of intense turbulence, with several high-profile book deals cancelled after authors were accused of using AI. Writers of color have disproportionately faced these investigative accusations, while innocent authors live in fear of false positives from detection tools or being penalized for trying to sound non-AI. The Copyright and Future Dilemma US copyright law currently requires books to be human-authored to receive full protection, leaving publishers hesitant to embrace AI fully. While traditional publishers refuse to promise a complete ban, many in the industry remain committed to protecting human artists against a backdrop of growing market anxiety.

item.title: AI makes companies flatter, but also more bureaucratic
item.description: The Hidden Cost of Cheaper Oversight Large companies traditionally relied on a human chain of supervisors and managers to enforce rules and check compliance, a process naturally limited by time and labor costs. However, recent deployments of AI tools in chains like Xushengji, Yiguotang, and Bestore allow companies to automate daily store audits, analyze thousands of operational data points continuously, and catch deviations cheaply. The Shift from Hierarchy to Micro-Rule This technological leap creates a paradox of organizational flattening. While fewer managers and shorter approval chains make corporate charts look cleaner, AI bypasses traditional layers to enforce standards directly onto every minute action. What used to be periodic weekly checks turn into relentless daily tasks. Front-line workers must spend their time explaining minor anomalies, leaving less room for local adaptability and proactive problem-solving. Balancing Control and Exploration Organizational research shows that while algorithm-driven monitoring can improve baseline execution, heavy-handed digital control often reduces employee initiative and critical feedback. As companies become hyper-efficient at enforcing existing standards, they risk penalizing non-standard yet innovative attempts, ultimately sacrificing long-term adaptability for short-term compliance.

item.title: Vega C Rocket Launch Delayed to Christmas Due to Late Satellites
item.description: According to Avio CEO Giulio Ranzo, speaking during the company's third-quarter earnings call, the third Vega C launch of 2026 has slipped by two to three weeks from its initial early December schedule. The mission will carry six satellites for Italy's IRIDE Earth observation constellation, which were recently delivered to the Guiana Space Centre by air. Ranzo noted that payload delivery delays have repeatedly impacted Avio's launch schedule this year, preventing the company from conducting more than three launches so far. While Avio previously aimed for up to five launches in 2027, Ranzo tempered expectations during the November call, indicating a more gradual increase to four annual flights, dependent on customers meeting their spacecraft delivery timelines.

item.title: France launches a new literary prize for works created with AI
item.description:
The newly announced Prix Pascal in France aims to embrace AI in literature by rewarding works created in collaboration with artificial intelligence. The initiative arrives amid intense debate sparked by the case of Canadian-Haitian author Thélyson Orélien, whose novel was dropped from multiple prestigious literary awards and his Canadian publisher after he was accused of undisclosed AI use. Chaired by essayist Jacques Attali, the inaugural Pascal Prize invites unpublished authors to submit a French-language text of up to 300,000 characters.
To qualify, participants must be transparent about their tools, explicitly acknowledging whether they used Claude, Gemini, or ChatGPT. Furthermore, candidates are required to submit a technical file detailing the specific LLMs or AI agents used, accompanied by a two-page explanation describing 'the seed'—defined as a word, sentence, or number—that originally sparked the creative project.

item.title: Transient beta oscillations precede voluntary movement stopping in rats
item.description: Background Brain wave activity known as beta oscillations has long been linked to how we control and inhibit movement, but scientists have struggled to pin down their exact timing relative to when a movement actually stops. This confusion largely stems from traditional testing methods where the exact moment of stopping is hidden or covert. Details To clear this up, researchers recorded 32-electrode brain activity alongside the running speed of head-fixed rats as they stopped running on a treadmill. They observed that a single beta wave cycle reliably occurs in the left motor cortex about 200 milliseconds before the rat stops. Using information theory, the study shows that beta power holds clues about future speed, but only when the animal is actively planning to stop. When researchers artificially added small amounts of time jitter to mimic older testing methods, this clear brain-action link completely broke down. Impact Using machine learning, the team demonstrated that despite being a clear biological marker of stopping, this specific beta oscillation has limited practical use for real-time decoding of actions. This work proposes a fresh conceptual model for how the brain controls the physical stopping of actions.

item.title: Coherus cuts 30% of workforce to focus on esophageal cancer drug trials
item.description:
Coherus Oncology announced a 30% reduction in its workforce as the company scales back its broader cancer pipeline to focus specifically on esophageal indications for its investigational combination therapy.
Last month, Coherus reported phase 1b data for the combination of tagmokitug, a CCR8-targeting antibody, and its approved PD-1 blocker Loqtorzi. According to the company, the combination demonstrated a confirmed overall response rate of 75% in front-line esophageal squamous cell carcinoma patients, regardless of PD-L1 status. Chief Medical Officer Rosh Dias stated that the data suggest regulatory T cells are a critical driver of resistance, and that tagmokitug enhances PD-1 activity.
To align with this narrowed strategy, Chief Financial Officer Bryan McMichael reported that the workforce reduction and pipeline narrowing will lower core cash burn by $6 million to $7 million quarterly over the next two quarters. The company reported third-quarter revenue of $14 million for Loqtorzi, its FDA-approved treatment for nasopharyngeal carcinoma, and ended September with $83.6 million in cash. Coherus plans to maintain selected other trials, including a phase 1b study with Johnson & Johnson and an ongoing phase 2 trial in liver cancer, while aiming for financial self-sufficiency.

item.title: AbCellera drops its OX40 drug program following industry-wide setbacks
item.description: Background AbCellera was developing ABCL575, an antibody targeting the OX40 ligand intended to treat atopic dermatitis and other autoimmune conditions. While its phase 1 trial successfully met tolerability and pharmacokinetic goals, the company decided not to advance the candidate past this initial stage, citing external developments across the entire OX40 drug class. Industry Context The broader OX40 class has faced significant hurdles recently. Earlier in the year, Kyowa Kirin and Amgen halted clinical studies for rocatinlimab due to emerging malignancy concerns. Subsequently, Sanofi scrapped regulatory submission plans for amlitelimab, conceding it offered no meaningful therapeutic improvement despite originating from an expensive $1.1 billion acquisition. Conversely, some developers like Inhibrx Biosciences remain optimistic, reporting positive early results for cancer immunotherapy combinations. Pipeline Shift With the OX40 program shelved, AbCellera is shifting its internal focus toward other pipeline assets. Its lead candidate is now ABCL635, an NK3 receptor-targeting antibody for menopausal hot flashes, which recently achieved a phase 2 success and is positioned as a potential non-hormonal therapy competing with existing commercial options.

item.title: Experts fear Treasury's proposed China biotech investment ban will backfire on U.S. leadership
item.description: The Proposed Rules and Industry Anxiety The U.S. Department of the Treasury released a 163-page draft policy detailing how it plans to implement the COINS Act, which seeks to add pharmaceutical compounds to an outbound investment blacklist. While traditional cash-based licensing deals remain untouched, the proposal places ambiguous restrictions on equity investments, co-development deals, and joint ventures involving Chinese entities, leaving biopharma executives and trade attorneys struggling to define compliant behavior. The Threat of a 'Flying Blind' Strategy Industry heavyweights, including a coalition of prominent healthcare investors led by RA Capital, argue that the rules will backfire. By barring U.S. investors and drugmakers from engaging in equity and co-commercialization structures in China, American firms will lose vital visibility into the global clinical pipeline. Critics warn that European investors and multinational pharmaceutical companies—unbound by these strict rules—will scoop up promising Chinese assets, leaving U.S. players at a severe disadvantage. The 'Joint Venture' Riddle and Economic Security A major source of confusion is the Treasury's lack of a clear legal definition for 'joint ventures,' which threatens popular models like U.S.-based 'NewCos' formed around Chinese-licensed assets. Legal experts note that the broad scope reflects a shifting political reality where economic security is treated as national security. Although the industry is pushing for narrower definitions focused strictly on bioweapons or select agents, analysts suggest that policymakers are determined to protect U.S. technological leadership across the board, regardless of the compliance burden and potential chilling effect on cross-border R&D.

item.title: Production MLOps at GS Caltex with Amazon SageMaker Canvas
item.description:
According to AWS Machine Learning:
GS Caltex, a South Korean energy and chemical company, divides AI model development between process engineers and machine learning engineers. Process engineers build and validate models visually in Amazon SageMaker Canvas without writing code. Meanwhile, ML engineers configure Amazon SageMaker Pipelines for deployment and scheduled inference.
To bridge the gap between development and production, GS Caltex automated the handoff process. ML engineers previously spent about a week on integration tasks like setting data paths and connecting preprocessing jobs. With the new automated setup, they can deploy models within a few hours. The company now runs batch inference every 30 minutes, which eliminates the need to keep costly real-time prediction endpoints running continuously and lowers overall costs.

item.title: LlamaIndex v0.14.26 Release: Security Fixes and Dependency Updates Across Integrations
item.description:
Overview of v0.14.26
The LlamaIndex v0.14.26 release focuses primarily on maintenance, security hardening, and cross-integration consistency. It rolls out updates to a vast array of callback handlers, embedding providers, graph stores, and managed indices. Key Security and Core Updates
A major focus of this release is executing a Python security relock across integration uv.lock files without altering the base Python floors where unnecessary. Additionally, breaking changes were introduced to raise requires-python specifications for security fixes across various integrations. In the llama-index-core package, a fix was implemented to resolve a deprecation issue that was breaking LangChain bridge imports.

item.title: Google Research releases Antigravity teamwork and Gemini 4 for scientific problem solving
item.description: According to Google Research: Background and Design Google Research details the design and applications of Antigravity's teamwork multiagent systems, built on top of various Gemini models including Gemini 4 Argon, Carbon, and Hydrogen. Frontier research requires navigating vast literature, building computational pipelines, and verifying every step. To address the unreliability of single model generations and the loss of context in multi-day tasks, teamwork uses parallel exploration paired with dedicated falsifiers like Lean 4 proof checkers and execution simulators, while partitioning context across specialized agents. Scientific and Engineering Results According to Google, teams across Google and academic institutions used these multi-agent workflows to solve long-standing open problems. In mathematics and theoretical computer science, researchers proved the 2013 Courtade–Kumar conjecture, resolved a 2014 open question in adaptive data analysis, and formalized complex proofs in Lean 4, including the Weil conjectures and parts of the Navier–Stokes equations. In systems software and hardware engineering, the tools were used to build the FarArray low-latency kernel-bypass system, rewrite large codebases like the Zircon microkernel and libgav1 into safe Rust, and optimize TPU kernels, yielding significant performance gains over manual implementations. Availability Google states that these features, along with the /boost command and Deep Review document evaluation tools, are currently available in Antigravity. Additionally, Google has opened applications providing 10,000 academic researchers with six months of free access to their highest usage tier.

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet for Secure Agent Payments
item.description: According to OpenAI News: Background and Partnership OpenAI reports that ChatGPT Wallet is built in partnership with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa. The feature is rolling out initially through dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US, aiming to help users complete purchases and give their agents a reliable way to pay. How It Works Users add their card once and can authorize their agent to pay. Before each purchase, the user reviews details and approves it using a security check like Face ID or fingerprint scan. After approval, the payment network provides a payment token instead of sharing actual card details with the business or agent. Impact on Businesses Agentic commerce is still in its early stages. OpenAI is releasing a Commerce Partner Playbook to help businesses adapt, ensuring websites do not inadvertently block agents and working with providers like Stripe and Adyen to reduce unnecessary declines.

item.title: Cloudflare's Kitesurf project is now open source
item.description: According to Cloudflare AI: Cloudflare has officially released Kitesurf as an open-source project. While the source text contains primarily website navigation menus and tag listings rather than a deep technical breakdown, the core announcement is the shift of Kitesurf toward open accessibility. Developers and community members can now explore its codebase, integrate it into various workflows, and contribute to its ongoing development.

item.title: Starship reaches orbit, but booster aborts landing and explodes in ocean
item.description: Flight Progress SpaceX launched its 15th Starship flight from Starbase, Texas, aiming to prove full reusability by recovering both rocket stages. The upper-stage Ship successfully reached orbit and deployed 26 Version 3 Starlink satellites, entering a planned long coast phase. Booster Abort The flight plan required the Super Heavy Booster 22 to return to the launch pad about 6.5 minutes after liftoff. However, it diverted to an offshore splashdown instead of attempting a tower catch. System Response According to SpaceX commentator Dan Huot, the vehicle's guidance, navigation, and control system triggered an automated abort because the booster was not where it needed to be for a safe catch. The booster subsequently exploded as remaining propellants burned off upon hitting the water, marking a setback for the Version 3 booster series.

item.title: Atom Computing Finalizes $100 Million U.S. Department of Commerce R&D Award
item.description: Background and Details Atom Computing has officially finalized a funding agreement worth up to $100 million with the U.S. Department of Commerce, following a Letter of Intent announced earlier this year. The company focuses on neutral-atom quantum computing and plans to use the capital for in-house technology development, expanding parallel engineering and testbed infrastructure, and collaborating with supply chain partners to scale up manufacturing. Additional Progress and Impact In addition to the Department of Commerce award, Atom Computing recently advanced to Stage C of DARPA's Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, which carries potential funding of up to $300 million. The company highlights several technical milestones, including building a platform with over 1,000 qubits, demonstrating quantum error correction, and selling a commercial on-premises quantum computer to QuNorth in 2025.

item.title: Build a Robot Pick-and-Place Simulation with SimReady Assets
item.description:
The walkthrough outlines a step-by-step process for building a beverage can pick-and-place simulation using the UR17G arm, Robotiq 2F-140 gripper, and a soda can within Isaac Sim 6.2. According to the text, SimReady Central provides OpenUSD assets equipped with pre-defined simulation properties such as collisions, mass, and joint settings, validated against specific profiles like Robot-Body and Robot-Gripper.
Developers can rely on AI agents combined with Isaac Sim skills to automate tasks, including loading local USD files, inspecting joint limits, assembling the arm and gripper into a single articulation, and generating Python-based movement controls. The guide emphasizes pre-run behavior checks—such as verifying joint settings, testing small arm movements, and confirming that objects rest correctly on work surfaces without falling through—to ensure the virtual robot interacts accurately with its environment.

item.title: IEEE Spectrum Video Friday Highlights NASA's PROMISE Moon Rover and In-Space Assembly
item.description: This week's IEEE Spectrum robotics video compilation highlights several developments across space and terrestrial robotics. According to the report, NASA plans to send a nuclear-powered rover named PROMISE to the Moon's South Pole, utilizing spare and test-bed hardware from previous Mars missions. In space manufacturing, a Caltech payload under DARPA's NOM4D program successfully assembled a truss structure in orbit using a gantry robot and a reflective mesh. Terrestrially, Boston Dynamics tested a wheeled version of its Atlas humanoid, while Corvus Robotics showcased autonomous inventory drones operating without localized infrastructure at an ASICS distribution center.

item.title: langchain-openai==1.8.0 - Dropping Python 3.10 Support and Adding OpenAIClassifier
item.description:
Version Update Details
The langchain-openai maintainers announce the release of version 1.8.0, which includes several key updates for developers building applications with language models. The most notable change is that Python 3.10 support has been dropped because it reached its end-of-life, making Python 3.11 the new minimum requirement. Users staying on older Python environments will automatically stick with the 1.7.x branch. New Features and Improvements
Beyond environment adjustments, this release introduces the OpenAIClassifier designed for the Generally Available Decisions API. Additionally, the team refreshed internal model profile data to ensure better compatibility and performance with recent updates.

item.title: NASA's Chandra Reveals the Secret Behind a Massive Star's Outbursts
item.description: According to NASA News: The Discovery Astronomers using NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory have solved the mystery behind AT 2016blu, a massive and unstable star located in the spiral galaxy NGC 4559, approximately 30 million light-years from Earth. The star is estimated to be at least 33 times the mass of our Sun. The Mechanism For over 15 years, scientists have observed this giant star brightening and dimming in optical light. Based on new X-ray observations, researchers suggest that the star has a previously hidden companion object, which is either a stellar mass black hole or a neutron star. As the two objects orbit each other, the companion pulls material from AT 2016blu every 113 days, causing the captured material to heat up and shine brightly in X-rays.

item.title: Six AGIBOT G2 Robots Complete 1,730 Tasks in 24-Hour Shanghai Convenience Store Trial
item.description: Real-World Retail Trial According to AGIBOT, six G2 wheeled humanoid robots were put to work in an active convenience store in Shanghai's Xuhui District for a continuous 24-hour period. The trial covered various shifts, including the lunchtime rush, evening peak hours, overnight operations, and the morning breakfast rush. During this time, the robots executed 1,730 tasks, ranging from customer service interactions and product pickups to coffee preparation, shelf inspections, and store cleaning. Testing Precision and Adaptability Operating in a live store presented everyday challenges that controlled laboratories cannot fully replicate. The G2 robots were subjected to practical evaluations, such as distinguishing between regular and sugar-free Coca-Cola, returning misplaced chewing gum to correct positions, and navigating around obstacles like people and boxes blocking the aisles. AGIBOT notes that four out of the six robots passed the final evaluation, which assessed duty time, task completion, customer feedback, and response times. Genie Master Framework To coordinate the fleet, AGIBOT utilized its Genie Master embodied AI agent framework. The system links task planning, execution, and feedback through an Embodied Execution Protocol, allowing the robots to learn from successful and unsuccessful attempts. AGIBOT plans to continue testing its robots in additional real-world environments to improve reliability and task execution.

item.title: LangChain Raises $300M Series C at $3B Valuation
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
LangChain announced that it has raised $300 million in Series C funding at a valuation of $3 billion, led by CapitalG with participation from GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures. The company believes that AI agents will transform the economy, and every enterprise will need to control its own intelligence, data, and infrastructure to build competitive advantages.
To capture this market, LangChain highlights its LangSmith platform, which serves over 7,000 organizations—including Fortune 500 enterprises like NVIDIA and Toyota as well as startups like Harvey. LangSmith is structured around three core pillars: Agent Runtime (infrastructure and architecture for running agents), Agent Improvement (testing, monitoring, and automated optimization), and Agent Governance (centralized control over models, tools, and sensitive data). The company also announced an upcoming release event scheduled for Friday, November 20th, to introduce new platform capabilities.

item.title: HHS pumps up to $25M into ibogaine, other psychotropic drugs on Veteran’s Day
item.description:
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services announced up to $25 million in investments targeting psychotropic compounds, with a particular focus on the psychedelic substance ibogaine. ARPA-H is allocating up to $4.9 million over five years for investigational medicines addressing PTSD, with subsequent awards slated for substance use disorders. Meanwhile, the National Institute of Mental Health is launching a $20 million funding opportunity for a research network examining treatments like ketamine, psilocybin, and esketamine.
Ibogaine has been a central focus of the Trump administration, supported by an executive order in April aimed at accelerating psychedelic therapies. Researchers note that ibogaine operates through a complex matrix pharmacology rather than a single target. While proponents highlight promising anecdotal and preliminary findings, the compound is also associated with neurotoxic and cardiotoxic risks, with published literature recording 33 deaths following its use as of 2022.

item.title: OpenAI and Databricks partner to bring enterprise AI to governed data
item.description: According to Databricks: Background OpenAI and Databricks have announced a multi-year partnership to connect OpenAI's advanced AI models directly with the governed data stored in Databricks. According to the companies, this aims to bridge the gap between powerful AI capabilities and corporate data context, addressing the common issue where AI lacks access to internal business definitions. Key Details The integration introduces three main adoption patterns. First, business users can query company metrics directly in ChatGPT using the Databricks Genie plugin, which applies the company's approved definitions and access rules. Second, engineering teams can use OpenAI Codex managed by the Databricks Unity Gateway, allowing leaders to control budgets and track usage. Third, developers can build custom AI agents using the OpenAI Agents SDK and deploy them as Databricks Apps. Impact This partnership gives enterprises a unified way to deploy AI across business intelligence, software engineering, and automated workflows while maintaining strict governance and security controls. Both companies are also customers of each other, with OpenAI utilizing Databricks and Databricks equipping its engineers with Codex.

item.title: Southern Co. considers $100 billion spending plan for natural gas, nuclear, and other investments
item.description:
During a third-quarter earnings call, Southern Co. executives outlined plans that could expand their baseline capital expenditure to $100 billion, up from an earlier $81 billion plan. The company reported a 3.5% year-over-year increase in weather-normalized electricity sales for the third quarter, with commercial sales jumping 7.3%. This growth is heavily anchored by data center usage, which surged 59% during the quarter.
To meet this rising demand, the company has accumulated a portfolio of 21 GW of signed large-load contracts across states like Alabama, Georgia, and Mississippi. Company leaders downplayed concerns that recent midterm election results and political debates over electricity costs would disrupt their plans, emphasizing that their signed agreements include strict minimum-bill provisions ensuring full cost recovery prior to power delivery.

item.title: Cellectis to cut 70% of workforce in strategic pivot to in vivo therapies
item.description: Strategic Pivot Cellectis announced in its third-quarter financial results that it will cut global headcount by up to 70% through 2026 and 2027. This reorganization follows the company's September decision to scrap its clinical-stage allogeneic CAR-T treatments, lasme-cel and eti-cel, due to shifting commercial and clinical landscapes. Pipeline Shift The Paris-based biotech is now reallocating its resources toward preclinical in vivo candidates, specifically HEAL-101 for severe hypertriglyceridemia and HEAL-201 for severe hypercholesterolemia. CEO André Choulika noted that preclinical data for HEAL-101 showed strong gene editing rates in humanized liver models, with initial clinical trials targeted for China. Industry Trend This move mirrors a broader industry trend where major pharmaceutical companies and biotechs are moving away from traditional ex vivo cell therapies. Competitors like Gilead's Kite Pharma, AbbVie, and Eli Lilly have recently made multi-billion-dollar investments and acquisitions to secure in vivo therapy pipelines.

item.title: LG Energy Solution scales up ESS strategy to target AI data center power demand
item.description:
As the global energy storage market shifts from small-scale renewable balancing to a critical component of power infrastructure, LG Energy Solution is focusing on grid-scale ESS and next-generation power solutions for AI data centers (AIDCs). Chang Beom Kang, Head of the ESS Battery Division, outlines the company's strategy in a recent Q&A, highlighting how hyperscalers are prioritizing 'Speed to Power' and driving demand for turnkey solutions, uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), and battery backup units (BBUs).
To capture this market, LG Energy Solution is leveraging its North American production network, which includes wholly owned and joint-venture sites, with ESS production capacity in the region expected to reach around 70 GWh by the end of next year. The company is also promoting its AEROS software suite for site optimization and preparing to showcase new products at RE+ 2026, including the JF3 LINK integrated LFP system and a concept combining Solid-State Transformers with sodium-ion batteries.

item.title: Release v5.23.0 - New Model Additions and Exporters Update
item.description:
New Model Additions
This release adds support for several prominent model families. Inkling2 is a multi-modal model supporting text and image inputs with a large parameter scale. Liquid AI's LFM3 and LFM3-VL introduce hybrid architectures combining gated short convolutions and grouped-query attention. Other notable additions include IQuestCoder for code generation, Shanghai AI Laboratory's InternLM3 instruction-tuned model, and experimental decision heads like JEV. Exporters and Backend Runtimes
The update brings a major overhaul to model exports. Every export now returns an ExportedModel, which shares the same API as the original model and can be pushed to the Hub and reloaded. It supports Dynamo, ONNX Runtime, OpenVINO, and ExecuTorch, with built-in runtime fusions that make decoding significantly faster than standard PyTorch eager execution. Core Bugfixes and Optimizations
Beyond new models, version 5.23.0 addresses a wide range of issues across vision pipelines, distributed training, attention mechanisms, caching, and audio processing. These include fixing cache correctness in various models, optimizing expert parallelism, and improving overall stability for multi-GPU setups.

item.title: 5 food and beverage companies making sustainable packaging changes
item.description:
Food and beverage manufacturers are facing mounting pressure from new extended producer responsibility laws and shifting consumer preferences, leading to practical updates in product packaging.
Several major brands have recently implemented specific material swaps. Campbell's replaced plastic dog bone packaging with a recyclable paper clip for Rao's sauce jars, removed mixed-material layers in its plastic bottles, and added recycled content to its pretzel canisters. PepsiCo reduced its overall plastic use by over 7 million pounds by lightweighting Gatorade and Lipton bottles. Target eliminated carbon-black colorant from its bakery and deli trays to make them more compatible with existing recycling systems. Bel Group swapped the outer cellophane wrap of Babybel cheese for paper to save an estimated 850 metric tons of packaging material annually globally. Meanwhile, Mars partnered with Berry Global to transition large M&M's, Skittles, and Starburst pantry jars to 100 percent post-consumer recycled plastic, aiming to eliminate over 1,300 metric tons of virgin plastic each year.

item.title: llama.cpp reaches v1.0.0, establishing a stable API for local AI development
item.description:
After three and a half years of growth, the llama.cpp project has become a foundational tool for running multi-modal large language models locally on everything from consumer computers to enterprise servers. With the release of version 1.0.0 for both llama.cpp and its tensor library ggml, the team aims to provide a more reliable foundation for the expanding ecosystem of local AI applications.
To support this growth, the project is establishing strict semantic versioning rules. Any breaking changes to the public C application programming interface will now trigger major version bumps, making interface boundaries clearer for developers who integrate the software into their products. Additionally, the project continues to expand its distribution channels and hardware support, utilizing infrastructure from Hugging Face alongside hardware partnerships with major chipmakers to ensure code quality and broad platform compatibility.

item.title: Marea Touts Phase 2 Lipid Disorder Win for MAR001
item.description: Clinical Results Cardiometabolic biotech Marea Therapeutics, now a subsidiary of Lisata Therapeutics following a September acquisition, released data from the first part of a phase 2b study evaluating its drug candidate MAR001. According to the company, the angiopoietin-like protein 4 (ANGPTL4)-targeting monoclonal antibody reduced triglycerides by 72.2% in patients with levels at or above 500 mg/dL, and by 57.2% in those at or above 300 mg/dL. More than half of the 235 adult patients on MAR001 reached normal triglyceride levels, compared to 3.4% on placebo. Treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in 69.5% of MAR001-treated patients, slightly below the 77.6% rate for the placebo cohort. Pipeline and Future Plans Marea CEO Josh Lehrer stated in an interview that the data is encouraging for establishing an optimal treatment for patients facing the dual threat of pancreatitis and cardiovascular risk. The company has already initiated the second part of the mid-stage study involving 100 patients, and plans to take a half-life-extended version called MAR005 into a phase 3 study for severe hypertriglyceridemia. Additionally, Marea is exploring the potential for its pipeline to address obesity and has a candidate named MAR002 in early-stage trials for acromegaly. Background The acquisition of Marea followed Lisata's failed deal with Kuva Labs, which resulted in significant workforce reductions. The subsequent merger with Marea involved a stock-for-stock transaction backed by a $225 million commitment from investors including Forbion, venBio, and Third Rock Ventures.

item.title: Delix raises $100M for depression drug without psychedelic trips
item.description: Background Delix Therapeutics, a Boston-based biotech born from a University of California lab in 2019, focuses on developing neuroplastogens, a class of drugs aimed at regrowing lost brain connections without causing traditional psychedelic trips. Details The newly raised $100 million Series C round was led by J&J's venture arm, with participation from several other investors. The funds will primarily advance its lead oral candidate, zalsupindole, which is based on a naturally occurring compound found in plants and toad secretions. Delix reported positive Phase 1b safety data in healthy volunteers in late 2024 and aims to launch a Phase 2b trial for major depressive disorder in the first half of 2027. Impact Beyond depression, the capital will support the pipeline's expansion into other neurological and neurodegenerative conditions, such as schizophrenia and Alzheimer's disease. The deal arrives amid renewed industry momentum, highlighted by recent high-profile acquisitions and regulatory focus on psychedelic-based mental health treatments.

item.title: Merck’s MASH drug efinopegdutide succeeds in mid-stage trial
item.description: Clinical Trial Results Merck revealed data from its phase 2b trial involving 386 patients with MASH and stage F2 or F3 fibrosis. Participants received one of three doses of efinopegdutide or a placebo for 52 weeks. The trial met its primary endpoint, showing MASH resolution in 56% to 63% of patients across the different doses, compared to 13% for the placebo arm. Drug Mechanism and Context Efinopegdutide is a subcutaneously injected co-agonist targeting both GLP-1 and glucagon receptors. Merck included a research arm using Novo Nordisk's semaglutide, where 53% achieved MASH resolution. Merck originally licensed the drug from Hanmi Pharmaceutical in 2020 after it passed through Johnson & Johnson's pipeline.

item.title: Cohere Expands Sovereign AI Platform with AISLE and cubic
item.description: According to Cohere Blog: Background and Acquisitions Cohere states that organizations increasingly require AI systems that are powerful, secure, and under their control, a concept the company refers to as sovereign AI. To advance this goal, Cohere has completed its acquisition of AISLE, a builder of autonomous systems for vulnerability discovery and remediation, and welcomed the team behind cubic, an AI-powered code review platform. These transactions mark Cohere's fourth and fifth strategic M&A deals this year, following Aleph Alpha and Reliant AI. Cybersecurity and Prague Hub Following the acquisition, AISLE co-founders are taking key leadership roles: Ondrej Vlcek becomes Senior Vice President of Cohere Cyber, Jaya Baloo becomes Chief Information Security Officer, and Stanislav Fort becomes Vice President of AI Security. Cohere plans a long-term investment in Prague, establishing the city as its global center for AI cybersecurity and autonomous security systems, leveraging AISLE's expertise to build cyber-resilient AI capabilities. Secure Coding and Enterprise Scale Cubic's team, led by founder and CEO Paul Sanglé-Ferrière, brings expertise in AI, security, and developer tools. Their review agents support environments such as on-premises and air-gapped deployments. According to Cohere, this team will establish the company's secure coding vertical, accelerating the integration of enterprise-grade coding and vulnerability remediation capabilities into its platform.

item.title: Regeneron's antibody curbs POTS heart rate spikes in mid-stage trial
item.description: Clinical Trial Results Regeneron reported data from its Phase 2 Pinnacle trial evaluating baloncibart, also known as REGN7544, in 82 patients with postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome (POTS). Patients receiving a 450-mg injection experienced a mean drop in heart rate of 11.4 beats per minute compared to placebo at day eight, while a 150-mg dose reduced heart rate by 9.5 beats per minute. The high-dose group also showed sustained heart rate reductions and reported improvements in physical functioning at day 29. Mechanism and Development POTS is a chronic autonomic nervous system disorder associated with lightheadedness and fatigue, with no currently approved treatments. Baloncibart is an NPR1-blocking monoclonal antibody designed to increase blood volume in circulation. Regeneron plans to launch a Phase 3 study in the first half of 2027, building on this mid-stage success.

item.title: Robot Talk: Making robots work reliably in high-risk environments
item.description: Real-World Challenges Daniela Shchegelskaya, an engineer from the University of Twente, shares her work on moving autonomous robots from controlled labs into unpredictable real-world settings. She highlights that reliability, connectivity, and system-level design are the biggest hurdles when deploying machines where failure is not an option. Substation Inspections At Elimpus, Shchegelskaya focuses on integrating Boston Dynamics' Spot robot to inspect live power substations. This involves enabling autonomous navigation, remote diagnostics, and data collection in environments with heavy electromagnetic interference and strict safety requirements.

item.title: Biopharma industry looks beyond GLP-1s for next-gen weight loss treatments
item.description: Amylin Pipeline Competition As existing GLP-1 treatments like Wegovy and Zepbound face challenges regarding side effects and plateauing results, amylin analogs are emerging as a primary alternative. Companies such as Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, and a partnership between Roche and Zealand Pharma are showcasing data for their pipeline assets, balancing higher efficacy against tolerability trade-offs. Muscle Preservation and Quality Beyond raw weight loss numbers, companies are prioritizing body composition. Biohaven and Wave Life Sciences are presenting data on therapies designed to target myostatin and INHBE proteins, aiming to reduce fat while preserving lean muscle, addressing a major drawback of current incretin drugs. Persistence and Long-Term Value Industry leaders note that roughly half of patients drop out of treatment within six months. Presentations at the conference, including Rhythm Pharmaceuticals' long-term data, highlight the growing importance of treatment durability and persistence in determining the true commercial and clinical value of obesity therapeutics.

item.title: How Dyania Health's AI speeds up patient chart reviews in hospitals
item.description: According to NVIDIA Generative AI: How Synapsis AI Works Hospitals accumulate vast amounts of patient history in free-text formats like physician notes and operative reports. Dyania Health developed Synapsis AI to read across these scattered documents, connecting findings from years apart to answer complex clinical questions and surface actionable signals for care teams. Security and Local Processing To protect patient privacy, Synapsis AI operates entirely on NVIDIA-accelerated computing inside the health system's firewall. The platform is trained using NVIDIA NeMo libraries and optimized via TensorRT, allowing hospitals to process records onsite without sharing sensitive data externally. Real-World Application at Cleveland Clinic In a study involving over 7,800 aortic valve replacement patients between 2005 and 2021, Cleveland Clinic utilized Synapsis AI to review historical charts and build predictive models for valve deterioration and reintervention risks. According to the health system, this approach completes manual chart reviews that would otherwise take years, with clinicians retaining final decision-making authority.

item.title: UK Publishes Roadmap to Export Cultivated Meat to Non-EU Countries
item.description: Background The UK Food Standards Agency (FSA) and Food Standards Scotland have released a new export process map for cell-cultivated products destined for non-EU markets. This initiative stems from the FSA's Cell-Cultivated Products Sandbox Programme, a two-year government-funded effort running until February 2027 to develop safety standards and regulatory guidance for the sector. Key Details The newly published guidance breaks down the export process into nine practical steps. It addresses market eligibility, production standards, import and marketing requirements, export health certification, customs declarations with HMRC, and logistics such as maintaining cold chains and temperature controls. The FSA notes that cultivated biomass counts legally as a processed product of animal origin rather than standard meat. Industry Impact While this roadmap provides clarity for international trade, the FSA has yet to approve cultivated meat for human consumption in the UK, with several applications currently under review. Meanwhile, ongoing UK-EU trade negotiations regarding sanitary and phytosanitary agreements could soon impact local novel food regulations and approval timelines.

item.title: Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
item.description:
Jensen Huang’s resignation has caused anxiety in Israel, where Nvidia employs around 6,000 people and has deep roots following its 2019 acquisition of Mellanox. Local tech figures note that Huang personally drove the company’s heavy investment in the region, raising questions about whether his successor will maintain the same level of commitment. Interim CEO Colette Kress has deep ties to the region, and Israeli executives like Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan have been floated as potential successors.
Despite the local uncertainty, venture capitalists in Israel view the transition as a potential turning point for the broader AI industry. According to Vertex Ventures Israel General Partner Yanai Oron, slower decisions at Nvidia could give rivals an opening, though a broader slowdown in AI spending remains a risk. Selah Ventures founder Adi Levanon notes that while Huang's departure does not dismantle Nvidia's ecosystem, it might prevent the company from becoming a full-on monopoly, giving alternative chip and inference software developers a chance to prove their economic value.

item.title: Nvidia processors power Chinese AI data centre projects worth $3 billion despite US export controls: Report
item.description: Project Details According to a Reuters report, multiple regions in China have incorporated restricted Nvidia processors into their AI infrastructure plans. Projects using H100 and H200 chips span across Fujian, Shaanxi, Jilin, Inner Mongolia, and Gansu provinces, with investments ranging from billions of yuan. Some facilities, such as a computing cluster in Wuxi using H800 processors, are already operational, while institutions like Shenzhen University and Northwestern Polytechnical University have also made smaller chip purchases. Potential Impact The heavy reliance on restricted American technology exposes Chinese developers to significant supply disruptions, construction delays, and rising costs as Washington tightens export controls. Furthermore, developers might eventually be forced to redesign their facilities to accommodate domestically produced alternatives.

item.title: Raise3D Launches T450 and T700 FDM 3D Printers Alongside New Software and Post-Processing Hardware
item.description: Product Launch Details Raise3D has introduced the T450 and large-format T700 FDM 3D printers ahead of Formnext 2026. Both models share a CoreXY motion platform with four frame-mounted motors and TwinFlow high-flow extrusion technology, which feeds two filament paths into a single nozzle. The systems include Air Flow Manager 2 to adjust chamber temperatures up to 70°C, and feature fiber-ready nozzles reaching 420°C. Applications and Pricing According to CEO Edward Feng, the T450's build area enables applications like single-piece adolescent scoliosis braces. Raise3D also reported significant production time and weight reductions for battery cell transport trays. The T450 is priced at $4,999, with deliveries starting in December 2026, while the T700 is priced at $15,999, with deliveries expected by January 2027. Additional Hardware and Software Alongside the new printers, Raise3D announced a 100 mm build-height increase for its RMS220 SLS printer via a software update, and introduced the B520 automated sandblaster for polymer powder bed parts. These developments follow a recent $15 million funding round aimed at supporting product portfolio upgrades and market expansion.

item.title: Nvidia scandal: Howard Lutnick under pressure over alleged lack of action
item.description: 背景与事件起因 据美联社等多家媒体报道，英伟达联合创始人兼CEO黄仁勋于周四辞职，并由首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯担任临时CEO。此前有报道称，黄仁勋卷入多起婚外情，其中包括与涉嫌中国间谍的艾丽斯·黄（Alice Huang）的关系。随着美国情报部门的相关报告在特朗普政府高层流传，舆论风暴迅速升级。 商务部长的压力 批评矛头直指美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克。多位国会议员指出，商务部在将与艾丽斯·黄有关联、且曾购买数十亿美元英伟达芯片的新加坡公司Megaspeed列入出口管制黑名单一事上存在拖延行为。白宫官员目前正在讨论是否应将卢特尼克撤职，而他本人已同意在未来几周内出席国会听证会。 行业与政策影响 这起丑闻正值美国收紧对华人工智能芯片出口的关键时刻。多位国会领袖呼吁彻底调查并堵住出口管制漏洞，而中国AI公司正试图在海外寻找替代芯片产能，北京方面也在加速推进以华为为代表的国产芯片替代进程。同时，黄仁勋在中国的巨大影响力和个人崇拜现象也在社交媒体上引发了广泛关注和讨论。

item.title: Oura's acquisition of Counsel Health raises conflict-of-interest concerns for Eli Lilly
item.description:
Smart ring maker Oura announced its acquisition of Counsel Health, a telehealth startup that connects patients with clinicians for popular GLP-1 weight-loss drug prescriptions. Previously, pharmaceutical giant Eli Lilly featured Counsel Health on its curated list of provider options for patients seeking these treatments. Conflict Concerns
According to industry experts, the transaction raises conflict-of-interest questions for Eli Lilly and similar drugmakers. By integrating hardware tracking with direct telehealth diagnosis and prescription services under one corporate umbrella, the acquisition blurs the lines between objective health data collection and commercial treatment pathways, prompting a closer look at how pharmaceutical companies partner with digital health platforms.

item.title: Jensen Huang Steps Down as NVIDIA CEO
item.description:
NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang has resigned from his positions as president, CEO, and board member after leading the company for 33 years since its founding in 1993. Following the announcement, the company's stock experienced a significant drop in pre-market trading before recovering slightly.
Executive Vice President and CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO while maintaining her current financial responsibilities. Kress has been with NVIDIA for over 13 years and previously held financial leadership roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Additionally, the board appointed Harvey C. Jones as NVIDIA's first-ever board chairman. The company confirmed that its Q3 fiscal 2027 earnings will be released on November 17 as originally scheduled.

item.title: ESA clarifies Prometheus engine tests are separate from Themis rocket delays
item.description: Engine Testing Update ArianeGroup announced that a series of hot-fire tests for the latest Prometheus rocket engine were completed on October 29 at DLR's P5 test bench in Lampoldshausen. According to the company, these tests were carried out independently of preparations for the Themis reusable booster demonstrator. A primary goal of this late-October campaign was to validate a new combustion chamber produced through a Cold Gas Spray additive manufacturing process, which aims to reduce production time and costs. Themis Flight Delays Meanwhile, the inaugural flight of the Themis reusable booster remains significantly delayed. Although officials previously targeted early 2026 for the first hop test from the Esrange Space Centre in Sweden, the vehicle remains grounded as winter approaches. During an October press conference, ESA's Director of Space Transportation stated that operators would decide by late November whether a 2026 inaugural flight is still feasible before winter weather halts testing.

item.title: US Lawmakers Summon Ex-Nvidia CEO After Spy Scandal
item.description:
Following the resignation of Nvidia's long-time leader after reports of extramarital affairs, US lawmakers have moved quickly to demand answers. Republican Senator Tim Scott requested that the former CEO and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick testify before the Senate Banking Committee in December, while three House committees also called for a closed-door interview.
Reports allege that one of the individuals involved was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security, raising serious concerns regarding the protection of sensitive US technology. The unfolding situation has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation, thrown the company into leadership transition with CFO Colette Kress serving as interim CEO, and left the broader AI industry navigating uncharted political and security waters.

item.title: AI's Next Phase: Why Companies Need New Organizational Structures
item.description: The Productivity Paradox While global enterprises are projected to spend over 250,000 million dollars on AI in 2025, only a small fraction report true business transformation. Robin Li compares this to the early days of electrification, noting that companies have installed new electric motors but have yet to redesign their factories. Moving to Intelligent Organizations Traditional corporate structures rely on human-centric hierarchies that act as information bottlenecks. To truly unleash AI capabilities, companies need to shift toward task-centered networks where humans collaborate with AI agent teams. Practice and Implementation Baidu reports internal successes by breaking down departmental boundaries, allowing employees to leverage AI to handle end-to-end tasks. Furthermore, platforms like Baidu's enterprise solutions aim to help companies capture tacit knowledge, build reusable skills, and utilize flexible model trading systems like 'Ciyuansuo' to power their evolving workflows.

item.title: Siemens Launches Intelligence Center X to Orchestrate Industrial AI
item.description: According to Siemens Blog: Keynote Overview At the Realize LIVE Americas 2026 event in Detroit, Siemens Digital Industries Software Executive Vice President Joe Bohman outlined the company's strategy to unify its software portfolio around a comprehensive digital twin. His keynote focused on five pillars: software-defined products, the updated Simcenter, Intelligence Center X, the Factory of the Future, and cloud integration. Technology Details According to Siemens, Intelligence Center X acts as an industrial AI orchestration layer. It integrates Mendix for agentic development, Graph Studio for graph databases, and AI Studio for machine learning, all underpinned by an industrial ontology layer. This architecture connects data across Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems. Practical Demonstration During the keynote, Bohman showcased a landing-gear replacement scenario to demonstrate the platform's capabilities. Siemens reports that the system can identify affected parts and recommend lower-risk alternatives in seconds instead of days, emphasizing that reliable enterprise data is a prerequisite for effective industrial AI applications.

item.title: Abstention Is Not Threshold Compliance: Stated Scoring Rules in Open Language Models
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: This paper investigates the proposal by Kalai et al. to use explicit probability thresholds in prompts as scoring rules, directing language models to answer only when their confidence exceeds threshold t. The authors probe 12 checkpoints across three post-training stages from four open 3-8B model recipes, alongside exploratory models up to 32B. The empirical tests reveal that while a strict abstention format line shifts mean abstention from 20% to 91% at t = 0.75, varying t from 0.5 to 0.9 within this format changes abstention by a mere -0.8 percentage points. Without formatting prompts, higher thresholds can paradoxically lower abstention, with up to 40% of items receiving decisions incompatible with threshold-independent beliefs. Furthermore, external thresholds on recalibrated P(True) showed brittle generalization across datasets like TriviaQA and PopQA, and models trained on threshold-conditioned targets failed to track unseen thresholds consistently. The study concludes that high abstention rates do not imply true rule compliance and outlines rigorous evaluation criteria for stated scoring rules.

item.title: Zugwise: Domain-Aware Game Reconstruction for Digitizing Handwritten Chess Scoresheets
item.description: The authors report in this preprint: Digitizing handwritten chess scoresheets has traditionally been framed as a handwriting-recognition task combined with move legality checks.
